validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed by 3 independent, non-GEM sources. (1) www.cdu.ru (Russian TEK/CDU energy-statistics agency page 'Gas industry of Tajikistan') explicitly names the pipeline: 'На балансе «Таджиктрансгаза» находятся: магистральные газопроводы... газопроводы «Келиф — Душанбе»' (Tajik Transgaz holds the Kelif-Dushanbe gas pipeline on its balance sheet) -- this is the sheet's own cited Status/Fuel/PipelineType ref and it DOES name this pipeline (the automated existing_ref_check flagged Status as 'value not found' only because it searched for the literal English string 'operating' on a Russian-language page -- that is a checker false negative, not a sourcing gap). (2) ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Келиф states 'В 1975 году через Келиф прошёл газопровод из Афганистана в Душанбе. Для него через Амударью был построен уникальный подвесной газопровод' (in 1975 a gas pipeline from Afghanistan to Dushanbe passed through Kelif; a unique suspended crossing was built over the Amu Darya for it) -- independently corroborates the 1975 build year and the Kelif waypoint. (3) ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Экономика_Таджикской_ССР: 'Таджикистан снабжался газом из Узбекистана, Афганистана (газопровод Келиф — Душанбе)' -- names the pipeline again as the Afghanistan-via-Kelif supply route to Tajikistan. DUPLICATE CHECK vs P6936 (Kelif-Mubarek): a 2003 RIA Novosti article (ria.ru/20030114/298122.html, on Turkmen-Uzbek gas talks) names them as two SEPARATE pipeline sections in one sentence: 'участков магистрального транзитного газопровода Мубарек-Келиф и Келиф-Душанбе' (sections of the trunk transit pipelines Mubarek-Kelif AND Kelif-Dushanbe) under discussion for transfer to Turkmenistan. This is the Kazakhstan cluster-A lesson applied correctly: an independent, non-GEM source affirmatively describes these as two distinct assets, so P6937 is NOT a duplicate/relabel of P6936 despite the shared Kelif endpoint and shared corridor family. Endpoints (Kelif, Turkmenistan -> Dushanbe, Tajikistan) match all three sources; CountriesOrAreas correctly carries all three transit states (Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan), which is why this multi-country row is properly in the Uzbekistan-gas scope despite neither endpoint being in Uzbekistan. | POLICY (source_roster.md: Wikipedia is never cited directly; studfile.net is a tertiary re-upload host, same class as the blocklisted wikidot). The Kelif / Tajikistan economy pages cited here are EVIDENCE for this concern, not a proposed [ref] cell, and the concern stands on its merits. But before the correction is applied to the sheet the geographic fact needs a citable source (GeoNames or the Uzbek statistics committee) — do not paste a Wikipedia URL into a [ref] cell.

fills.researcher_notes: Genuine best-effort search in Russian first, per scope guidance. cdu.ru (TEK Russia) confirms Tajik Transgaz as the balance-holder/operator of the Kelif-Dushanbe line on Tajik territory -- only ONE of the three named operators. Uztransgaz appears there only as Tajikistan's gas SUPPLIER (a 2018 import contract), not named as pipeline operator; a separate search (Interfax 2012 wire item on a Uztransgaz-Tajik Transgaz supply contract) is the same supplier relationship, not an operator confirmation. Found nothing naming Turkmengaz as operator of the Turkmen segment specifically. Historical context (RIA Novosti 2003) shows Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan negotiating transfer of pipeline SECTIONS between each other, consistent with a multi-operator segmented asset, but that is 2003-vintage and about a proposed transfer, not a current operator confirmation. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than citing mfa.gov.tm (checked and found irrelevant to this pipeline, see validity note) or fabricating corroboration for Uztransgaz/Turkmengaz as operators. This tracks the country's calibration: a genuine Russian-language search that comes up short on a state-monopoly-operated asset is an honest UNRESOLVED, not a failure to look.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=operating is supported but needs a caveat about WHICH gas is flowing, not whether the pipe carries gas at all. cdu.ru confirms the line sits on Tajik Transgaz's active operated network. The Times of Central Asia (dated Aug 20-21, 2026 diplomatic visit) frames any TURKMEN gas reaching Tajikistan as still purely prospective: 'Any Turkmen gas bound for Tajikistan would have to pass through Uzbekistan... No prices, volumes, or timetable have been announced, leaving the plan on paper' -- and states Tajikistan's actual 2024 imports (~267 million cubic meters) were Uzbek gas, not Turkmen-origin gas. So the physical corridor is demonstrably in current use delivering gas to Dushanbe (2024 import volumes), which supports keeping Status=operating for the pipeline asset -- but there is no current evidence that gas is entering at the Kelif (Turkmenistan) end specifically; gem.wiki's own background section (read for leads only, not cited) similarly suggests the Turkmen segment may be idle while the Uzbek segment is what's actively moving gas. This is a Fuel-source/segment-flow question, not grounds for a Status change on this operating trunk -- verdict is CONFIRM, with the caveat flagged above for whoever next reviews FuelSource or considers splitting the row by country segment. Fergana.agency (Jan 2022) confirms Uzbekistan cut ALL gas exports briefly in winter 2021-22 for domestic shortage reasons, which is consistent with year-to-year supply variability on this corridor but not evidence of permanent closure -- 2024 import figures postdate that cut and show flow resumed.

summary: P6937 confirmed real and correctly distinct from P6936 (RIA Novosti 2003 names them as two separate sections); Status=operating confirmed with a caveat that current flow to Tajikistan is sourced as Uzbek gas rather than confirmed Turkmen-origin gas via Kelif. Two concerns staged: an attribution defect (OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName swapped between P6936/P6937, plus a partly irrelevant Owner [ref] URL) and a spec concern (LengthKnown 300 km vs the mapped route's LengthEstimateKm 406.14 km, 35% apart). Operator [ref] fill left UNRESOLVED -- only Tajik Transgaz is independently confirmed as operator; Uztransgaz/Turkmengaz co-operation not corroborated to standard.
